findings.description: No keyboard preview test exercises a non-null keyboardParseMode. The keyboard branch renders keyboardText through a DEDICATED code path (FunnelService.renderTextBlock → VariableTemplateRenderer.render(text, parseMode, subscriber), diff lines 36-39) that is SEPARATE from renderBlocks. The existing escaping tests (previewEscapesHostilePayload / previewMarkdownV2EscapesFullSet, lines 756/784) only cover the MESSAGE branch via renderBlocks, so they do NOT protect the keyboard branch. Every new keyboard test passes parseMode=null (previewKeyboardBody(..., null, ...)), so the keyboardParseMode→renderTextBlock wiring is unverified. Litmus test: if renderTextBlock hard-coded parseMode to null (dropping the keyboardParseMode argument), ALL current keyboard tests still pass — i.e. an HTML/XSS-escape regression on the keyboard preview ships green. This is the security-relevant AC ('escaping per keyboardParseMode', Acceptance Criteria line 96-98) and is currently untested.
findings.recommendation: Add a test previewSetKeyboardEscapesPerParseMode: seed a SET_KEYBOARD step, set firstName to a hostile value (e.g. owner.setFirstName("x")), POST previewKeyboardBody("SET_KEYBOARD", "Привіт {user.first_name}", "HTML", keyboardRow("Меню")), then assert jsonPath("$.renderedBlocks[0].text").value("Привіт <b>x</b>") and assert the raw response body does NOT contain the unescaped "" (mirror previewEscapesHostilePayload, line 756-782). Optionally also assert renderedBlocks[0].parseMode=="HTML" to pin the parseMode echo. This is the single missing test that makes the keyboard escaping AC enforceable.

findings.description: No keyboard test covers the sampleData=true stub-subscriber path. The keyboard branch reuses the same resolved subscriber/stub and sampleData flag as the message branch, and previewUnlinkedBotUsesStubSubscriber (line 812) covers it for MESSAGE — so this is partially covered transitively. However the keyboard branch independently echoes the sampleData flag into the new 4-arg PreviewStepResponse constructor; a stub-path keyboard test would pin that the flag is preserved on the keyboard branch specifically. Currently both keyboard tests that assert sampleData assert only the false (linked-owner) path (line 894); previewSetKeyboardClampsOversizedRows and previewClearKeyboardReturnsNullRows assert no sampleData at all.
findings.recommendation: Either add a keyboard variant that seeds NO owner subscriber (seedConnectedBot without owner) and asserts jsonPath("$.sampleData").value(true) with kind="keyboard" and a rendered stub name, OR accept transitive coverage from previewUnlinkedBotUsesStubSubscriber and document that the sampleData flag is branch-agnostic. Low priority — the message-branch stub test plus the keyboard sampleData=false test give reasonable confidence.

findings.description: Defensive null/blank edge cases enumerated in the task spec (4.md 'Edge cases', lines 192-198) have no direct test, despite the production code adding explicit guards for them (clampKeyboardLabels skips null rows / null buttons / null button text, diff lines 58-68; renderTextBlock renders null keyboardText null-tolerantly; null keyboardRows on SET_KEYBOARD returns null). These guards are dead-untested: (a) blank/null keyboardText still yields one TEXT block; (b) SET_KEYBOARD with keyboardRows omitted/null echoes keyboardRows=null (not an empty array); (c) a row containing a null button / null text is skipped without NPE. Litmus: deleting the 'if (row == null || row.buttons() == null) continue' / 'if (button == null || button.text() == null) continue' guards (diff 58, 66) would not fail any current test. The clamp test only feeds well-formed oversized rows.
findings.recommendation: Add (at least) previewSetKeyboardNullRowsEchoesNull: SET_KEYBOARD with previewKeyboardBody("SET_KEYBOARD","t",null) (no rows) → assert kind="keyboard", renderedBlocks.length()==1, jsonPath("$.keyboardRows").doesNotExist(). Add previewSetKeyboardBlankTextRendersOneBlock: keyboardText="" (or absent) → renderedBlocks.length()==1, renderedBlocks[0].text=="". The null-button-inside-row case is harder to express via the JSON helpers (keyboardRow can't emit a null button object); either extend previewKeyboardBodyRows to accept a raw row map with a null button entry and assert that row collapses, or accept that the guard is belt-and-suspenders DTO tolerance and document it as deliberately untested. The keyboardText-blank and null-rows cases are cheap and pin two explicit spec edge cases.

findings.description: previewSetKeyboardClampsOversizedRows bundles all three clamp dimensions (rows>10, buttons>4, label>64) into a single payload but asserts the label-truncation only on keyboardRows[0][0] ('x'.repeat(64)) and the row/button clamp only via length() counts. The row-count clamp to 10 and per-row button clamp to 4 are asserted (length()==10, [0].length()==4), which is adequate. The label clamp is asserted on exactly one label. This is acceptable single-concern-adjacent coverage, but a non-clamped boundary label (exactly 64 chars passes through unchanged) is not pinned, so an off-by-one in the truncation (e.g. substring(0,63) or substring(0,65)) is only caught for the >64 case, not the ==64 boundary.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add one assertion or a tiny test: a 64-char label survives verbatim (boundary), e.g. include keyboardRow with a label of exactly 'x'.repeat(64) on a separate non-clamped row and assert it equals 'x'.repeat(64) unchanged. Confirms truncation is '> MAX' not '>= MAX'. Low priority — the current >64→64 assertion already catches gross truncation bugs.

summary: Status: needs_improvement. The five new IT cases are well-constructed, meaningful integration tests with real assertions (rendered text with variable substitution, verbatim labels, clamp counts, null-rows discriminator, MESSAGE regression guard) — they pass the litmus test for the core happy-path contracts and directly cover four of the five TDD-Anchor cases plus the regression guard. No empty/mock-only/anti-pattern findings; pyramid is correct (IT is the right layer for this controller+service surface). One MAJOR gap: the keyboard branch's keyboardParseMode→escaping path runs through a dedicated renderTextBlock code path that NO keyboard test exercises with a non-null parse mode — the security-relevant 'escaping per keyboardParseMode' AC would pass even if parseMode were dropped (regression ships green). Three MINOR gaps: no keyboard stub-path (sampleData=true) test, and the spec-enumerated null/blank keyboardText + null-keyboardRows-on-SET_KEYBOARD defensive guards are untested (deleting those guards fails no test). Recommend adding previewSetKeyboardEscapesPerParseMode (the load-bearing fix) plus the cheap blank-text and null-rows cases.
